newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended stronger on a recovery in the bullion price and industrials were soft amid a lack of interest ahead of closed marekts for a Human Rights Day holiday on Friday.
Dealers said players were sceptical of the gold price trading above $355 per ounce but added that if that level was broken, then interest in golds would be rekindled.

"Golds are slightly better for choice. They would not react too much to this recovery in bullion because it is capped at $355. There is actually a good possibility that it will drift back to the early 50's or high 40's," a dealer said.
Industrials were weaker, much a result of a lack of interest after the March futures close-out on Monday. Dealers said the three four-day weeks were taking their toll on industrials.
Next week is also a four-day week with the Good Friday holiday closing markets, as well as the Easter Monday holiday.
"We will have to get the Easter holidays out of the way before we see much interest in industrials," one dealer said.
But dealers added that industrials would build a good base for themselves next week before rising ahead of the unit trust March quarter close-out at month-end.
"(The close-out) would bode well for continued strength in the industrial sector," Grahame Graham-Parker, general manager at Infinity Asset Management, told Reuters.
The all-share index was down 0.9 points to 7,098.6 points, the gold index gained 6.6 points to 1,832.2 points and the industrial index shed 20.0 points to 8,322.6 points.
Volumes traded were thin, excluding large corporate trades in De Beers, Liberty Life and Sasol.
Dealers said besides those three the market was quiet with interest in green chips from private as well as institutional investors.
De Beers added 75 cents to 159 rand, Liberty Life gained 75 cents to 124.75 rand, Iscor dropped 12 cents to 346 cents and RMB was up 125 cents to 103.75 rand.
Freegold added a rand to 35 rand, Kloof was up 15 cents to 34.15 rand and Rusplats was 150 cents to 72 rand.
Near-term gold equity futures ended stronger on a better bullion price while industrials were softer knocked by a weaker Wall Street overnight.
The June all-share contract was last at 6,571/80 from 6,555, the industrial contract was at 8,166/78 from 8,180 and the gold contract was at 975/80 from 980.
